item.base_system: Pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy powder
item.intervention: Additive manufacturing via Selective Laser Melting (SLM) using specific laser parameters
item.processing: Laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern
item.test_conditions: Room temperature and high temperatures (25 °C to 900 °C) compression tests
item.structure_change: Formed FCC single-phase random solid solution with epitaxial growth grains, dislocation networks, and nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates (27.3 nm)
item.property_change: Yield strength of 778.4 MPa at room temperature, significantly higher than annealed (254.2 MPa) and other AM-processed (519 MPa) HEAs
item.attributed_mechanism: Outstanding mechanical properties attributed to dislocation network, fine grain size, and nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates
quotes: SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
The room temperature compressive yield strength measured 778.4 MPa.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy powder. Intervention: Additive manufacturing via Selective Laser Melting (SLM) using specific laser parameters. Processing: Laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern. Test conditions: Room temperature and high temperatures (25 °C to 900 °C) compression tests. Structure change: Formed FCC single-phase random solid solution with epitaxial growth grains, dislocation networks, and nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates (27.3 nm). Property change: Yield strength of 778.4 MPa at room temperature, significantly higher than annealed (254.2 MPa) and other AM-processed (519 MPa) HEAs. Mechanism: Outstanding mechanical properties attributed to dislocation network, fine grain size, and nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates. Evidence: measured. Quote: "SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution."

item.intervention: Compression testing at elevated temperatures (500 °C to 900 °C)
item.processing: Compression tests at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C with initial strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹
item.structure_change: Slip and deformation twins observed from 25 °C to 600 °C; slip and partial recrystallization observed above 700 °C
item.property_change: Yield strength decreased from 756.5 MPa at 25 °C to 223.0 MPa at 900 °C, with a significantly smaller decrease up to 700 °C
item.attributed_mechanism: Superior mechanical properties up to 700 °C maintained by high dislocation density and fine precipitates; deformation mechanisms shift from slip/twinning to slip/recrystallization
quotes: SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA has superior mechanical properties up to 700 °C.

The major deformation mechanisms were slip and deformation twinning that occurred from room temperature up to 600 °C, and slip and partial recrystallization that occurred at temperatures higher than 700 °C.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: As-built SLM equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. Intervention: Compression testing at elevated temperatures (500 °C to 900 °C). Processing: Compression tests at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C with initial strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Test conditions: Temperatures ranging from 25 °C to 900 °C. Structure change: Slip and deformation twins observed from 25 °C to 600 °C; slip and partial recrystallization observed above 700 °C. Property change: Yield strength decreased from 756.5 MPa at 25 °C to 223.0 MPa at 900 °C, with a significantly smaller decrease up to 700 °C. Mechanism: Superior mechanical properties up to 700 °C maintained by high dislocation density and fine precipitates; deformation mechanisms shift from slip/twinning to slip/recrystallization. Evidence: measured. Quote: "SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA has superior mechanical properties up to 700 °C."

item.processing: Compressive deformation at 600 °C with low strain rate
item.structure_change: Type-C serration observed in stress-strain curve; activation energy measured at 335 kJ/mol
item.property_change: Stress drop amplitude (Δσ) measured as ~4.5 MPa during serrated flow
item.attributed_mechanism: Serrated flow related to cooperative lattice diffusion of constituent elements and interaction with nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates
quotes: The 600 °C compressive stress-strain curve, remarkably, showed type-C serration.
Activation energy measured 335 kJ/mol, which was significantly higher than the activation energy related to the diffusion of common interstitial solutes.
The serrated flow of SLM-built HEA can be uninfluenced by interstitial atoms, and this is related to the cooperative lattice diffusion of constituent elements.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. Intervention: Compression deformation at 600 °C. Quote: "The 600 °C compressive stress-strain curve, remarkably, showed type-C serration."

item.structure_change: Dynamic recrystallization (DRX) and dynamic recovery (DRV) observed; ultra-fine grains (378 nm) formed at grain boundaries; gDRX and dDRX mechanisms active
item.property_change: Work softening occurred; yield strength and flow stress reduction were greater at temperatures higher than 700 °C
item.attributed_mechanism: Dramatic decrease in flow stress above 700 °C attributed to DRX; Zener drag effect from oxides delays full recrystallization
quotes: Work softening occurred at temperatures higher than 700 °C.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. Intervention: Compression deformation at temperatures above 700 °C. Processing: Compressive deformation at 700 °C, 800 °C, and 900 °C. Test conditions: High temperature compression (700 °C to 900 °C). item.intervention: Analysis of dislocation density in as-built state
item.processing: Convolutional multiple whole profile (CMWP) analysis of XRD patterns
item.structure_change: Dislocation density calculated at 1.88 × 10¹⁴ m⁻², higher than homogenized HEA
item.property_change: Contributes to superior mechanical properties compared to homogenized HEA
item.attributed_mechanism: High dislocation density caused by thermal contraction strain during rapid solidification and cooling
quotes: This is a common tendency found in AM-processed materials, and it is known to be caused by thermal contraction strain that occurs during rapid solidification and cooling.

item.structure_change: Mn2O3 phase identified with average size of 27.3 nm at cell structure boundaries; no Cr-Mn-based oxide or σ-phase formed
item.property_change: Contributes to Orowan strengthening and delays recrystallization via Zener drag
item.attributed_mechanism: Nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates provide Orowan strengthening and increase Zener pinning pressure
quotes: Phases with an average size of 27.3 nm formed in the cell structure boundary.

Property change: Contributes to Orowan strengthening and delays recrystallization via Zener drag. Mechanism: Nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates provide Orowan strengthening and increase Zener pinning pressure. Evidence: measured. item.intervention: Texture analysis via EBSD pole figure
item.processing: EBSD pole figure analysis of Building Direction (BD)
item.structure_change: Strong <001> texture (10.12 MUD) developed along with <101> (4.52 MUD) and <111> (6.70 MUD) textures
item.property_change: Anticipated positive influence on mechanical properties due to <101> texture presence
item.attributed_mechanism: Texture development due to heat dissipation direction and scanning strategy control
quotes: The present alloy developed strong <001> texture as well as <101> and <111> textures.
The maximum intensity of multiples of uniform density (MUD) measured 10.12, 4.52 and 6.70, respectively, in <001>, <101> and <111>.
It is commonly known that if an FCC alloy develops <101> texture, it will have a greater strength and elongation compared to <001> texture.

item.structure_change: σ-phase formed at the cell structure boundary
item.property_change: No extreme flow stress decrease observed up to 900 °C
item.attributed_mechanism: Delayed recrystallization due to Zener drag from oxides and migrated grain boundaries
quotes: In the case of the sample deformed at 900 °C, σ-phase was formed at the cell structure boundary.
An extreme flow stress decrease does not occur in SLM-built HEA up to a condition of ~900 °C.
SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA is expected to delay strain softening up to 900 °C.

Test conditions: 900 °C compression. Structure change: σ-phase formed at the cell structure boundary. Property change: No extreme flow stress decrease observed up to 900 °C. Mechanism: Delayed recrystallization due to Zener drag from oxides and migrated grain boundaries. Evidence: measured. Quote: "In the case of the sample deformed at 900 °C, σ-phase was formed at the cell structure boundary."

item.test_conditions: Room temperature and high temperature ranges
item.structure_change: SLM-built HEA has unique microstructure (fine grains, dislocation network, nano-oxides) compared to conventional or other AM HEAs
item.property_change: Higher yield strength up to ~800 °C compared to EBM-built Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb gamma alloy; excellent high-temperature strength compared to oxide dispersion strengthened steels
item.attributed_mechanism: Multiple strengthening mechanisms (dislocation forest hardening and Orowan strengthening) remain effective at high temperatures
quotes: Compared to CoCrFeMnNi HEAs manufactured with other manufacturing processes, the SLM-built HEA has higher mechanical properties in room temperature as well as high temperature ranges.
When compared to oxide dispersion strengthened steels, which are developed by cryo-milling, SLM-built HEA represented excellent high-temperature strength at temperatures greater than 700 °C.
In high temperature conditions (above 700 °C), the outstanding high-temperature mechanical properties are achieved as σρ and σOr have a significant influence on strengthening.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. Intervention: Comparison with other manufacturing processes. Processing: Literature comparison of mechanical properties. Test conditions: Room temperature and high temperature ranges. Structure change: SLM-built HEA has unique microstructure (fine grains, dislocation network, nano-oxides) compared to conventional or other AM HEAs. Property change: Higher yield strength up to ~800 °C compared to EBM-built Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb gamma alloy; excellent high-temperature strength compared to oxide dispersion strengthened steels. Mechanism: Multiple strengthening mechanisms (dislocation forest hardening and Orowan strengthening) remain effective at high temperatures. Evidence: measured. Quote: "Compared to CoCrFeMnNi HEAs manufactured with other manufacturing processes, the SLM-built HEA has higher mechanical properties in room temperature as well as high temperature ranges."

item.processing: HR-EBSD analysis on sample deformed at 700 °C
item.structure_change: Ultra-fine grains (378 nm) found at grain boundaries; migration of high angle boundaries (HABs) observed; GND distribution shows dislocations are not new strain-free grains
item.property_change: Work softening begins; yield strength drop occurs
item.attributed_mechanism: DRX caused by combination of dDRX and gDRX involving accumulation, migration, and rotation of HABs
quotes: In the IPF map, ultra-fine grains with an average size of 378 nm were found at grain boundaries.
The DRX of SLM-built HEA is caused by combination of dDRX and gDRX, which follow the process of i) accumulation of dislocations at HABs, ii) migration or bulging of HABs, and iii) rotation of HABs.
gDRX, where flow stress continuously decreases by small amounts, is somewhat different with dDRX, where flow stress decreases sharply.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. Intervention: Deformation at 700 °C. Processing: HR-EBSD analysis on sample deformed at 700 °C. Test conditions: 700 °C compression. Structure change: Ultra-fine grains (378 nm) found at grain boundaries; migration of high angle boundaries (HABs) observed; GND distribution shows dislocations are not new strain-free grains. Property change: Work softening begins; yield strength drop occurs. Mechanism: DRX caused by combination of dDRX and gDRX involving accumulation, migration, and rotation of HABs. Evidence: measured. Quote: "In the IPF map, ultra-fine grains with an average size of 378 nm were found at grain boundaries."

item.structure_change: Large number of deformation twins (DTs) observed; work hardening continued; no dynamic recrystallization
item.property_change: Work hardening behavior observed; high yield strength maintained
item.attributed_mechanism: Work hardening due to dislocation suppression from increased dislocation density and DT evolution
quotes: A large number of deformation twins (DTs, θ ≈ 60°) were observed at room temperature.
In the true stress-strain curves, work hardening continued from room temperature up to 600 °C.
The reason why work hardening occurs at temperatures below 600 °C is suspected to be because dislocation is suppressed as a result of dislocation density increase and DT evolution.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. Intervention: Deformation at room temperature to 600 °C. Processing: Compressive deformation at 25 °C, 500 °C, and 600 °C. Test conditions: Low to medium temperature compression. Structure change: Large number of deformation twins (DTs) observed; work hardening continued; no dynamic recrystallization. Property change: Work hardening behavior observed; high yield strength maintained. Mechanism: Work hardening due to dislocation suppression from increased dislocation density and DT evolution. Evidence: measured. Quote: "A large number of deformation twins (DTs, θ ≈ 60°) were observed at room temperature."

item.processing: Electron channeling contrast (ECC) imaging and STEM-EDS mapping
item.structure_change: Cellular and columnar structures (~400 nm) decorated with dislocation networks; no elemental segregation observed in cells
item.property_change: Contributes to strengthening via dislocation network and fine precipitates
item.attributed_mechanism: Substructures formed by dislocation networks as compensation for distortions from thermal contraction stress
quotes: Scanning TEM (STEM)-EDS mapping of the cell structure confirmed that elemental segregation did not occur, and this leads to the conclusion that substructures in SLM-built HEA are only formed by dislocation networks.
This dislocation network can be understood as the compensation for distortions formed within the grain as a result of thermal contraction stress during fast cooling.

Mechanism: Substructures formed by dislocation networks as compensation for distortions from thermal contraction stress. Evidence: measured. Quote: "Scanning TEM (STEM)-EDS mapping of the cell structure confirmed that elemental segregation did not occur, and this leads to the conclusion that substructures in SLM-built HEA are only formed by dislocation networks."
